2023_038_m041823bdmtg.paragraph: Minutes of the Troy Board of Education regular meeting of April 18, 2023, held at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, called to order by President Schmidt at 7:00 p.m. with all seven members present and approximately 150 people in the audience. The Board approved four two-year probationary administrative contracts, awarded a gym floor renovation bid of $63,930.00 to Floor Care Concepts and an elementary audio upgrade bid of $498,676.00 to TelSystems, and authorized Superintendent Dr. Richard Machesky to negotiate a lease with the Troy Racquet Club for a tennis facility on the Troy High School site. That resolution carried 6 to 1, with Mrs. Alic dissenting.
2023_038_m041823bdmtg.page:
**Meeting and Attendance**
Regular meeting of the Troy Board of Education, April 18, 2023, Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois. President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. Present with Mr. Schmidt were Board members Alic, Anne, Hauff, Haupt, Philippart, and Wilson. Superintendent Machesky attended along with administrators Birmingham, DiPilato, Griffor, Detmer, Duda, Roncone, Jansen, Canfield, Griffin, Naus, Cottone, Young, Henry, Barsh, Keen, Recker, DiPonio, Keyser, Conaton, Harris, and West. Approximately 150 members of the audience were present. The meeting adjourned at 9:20 p.m.

**Recognitions**
President Schmidt changed the order of the Recognition items. The Mission Moment honored Leonard Elementary ASD teacher Megan Murray and Literacy Specialist Nancy Haboush for an adapted version of LLI intervention; Dr. Erin Detmer and Sarah Young introduced them. The Student Spotlight featured Grace Cafagna, a senior at Athens High School in the TSD Creative Guild, introduced by Thomas Butcher. Stefanie Gervais was named 2023 Outstanding Support Staff Employee of the Year from 25 nominees, with a reception set for May 11th. The Outstanding Teacher of the Year program drew 62 nominations; a reception for all nominees was set for April 25th.

| Outstanding Teacher 2023 | Position |
|---|---|
| Erich Beregszaszy | Science Teacher, Athens High School |
| Shannon Dziwanowski | Science Teacher, Larson Middle School |
| Patricia Grandy | Teacher, Troy Preschool |
| Karen Rosewarne | 5th Grade Teacher, Leonard Elementary School |

Mrs. Rosewarne was also selected Overall TSD Teacher of the Year for 2023. Winners were sent to Oakland Schools for the Countywide Outstanding Teacher Award program.

**Consent Agenda (23-024)**
Moved by Mr. Hauff, supported by Mr. Haupt; items A through F approved 7 yes, 0 no: minutes of the March 7, 2023 Workshop; minutes of the March 11, 2023 Retreat; minutes of the March 21, 2023 Board Meeting; Treasurer's Report for February 2023; Ancillary Fund(s) Budget Amendment; and rescheduling the June 20 Board meeting to June 13 at 7:30 pm at Troy High School.

**Personnel Actions (all effective July 1, 2023; all 7-0)**

| Res. | Appointee | Position | Mover / Support |
|---|---|---|---|
| 23-025 | Mr. Patrick Griffin | Principal, International Academy East | Wilson / Hauff |
| 23-026 | Ms. Gabrielle Naus | Assistant Principal, International Academy East | Anne / Philippart |
| 23-027 | Mr. John Pagel | Assistant Superintendent, Employee Services | Haupt / Alic |
| 23-028 | Mr. Brian Canfield | Director, Employee Services | Alic / Anne |

Each received a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure. Resolution 23-029 (Philippart / Wilson) approved elementary and secondary personnel recommendations including new hire Szczepanski, 7-0. Curriculum items: none.

**Business**
Resolution 23-030 (Alic / Hauff) awarded the THS gym floor renovation bid to Floor Care Concepts for $63,930.00, payable from the Building Site & Sinking Fund and/or the 2023 Bond Fund; 7-0. Resolution 23-031 (Hauff / Haupt) awarded Elementary Audio Upgrades to TelSystems for $498,676.00 from the 2023 Bond Fund; 7-0.

**Troy Racquet Club Partnership (23-032)**
Moved by Mrs. Anne, supported by Dr. Philippart. The resolution contemplates a tennis facility on the Troy High School site with 12-15 courts, up from the 8 that currently exist, domed approximately October through April, with outdoor lighting for later summer play. Play would be membership-based for community members and for students outside the school day; Troy High students and staff get free exclusive access during tennis sections of the Physical Education curriculum, district tennis programs get free in-season access, and TRC would provide free membership to students showing proof of economically disadvantaged status. Dr. Richard Machesky or his designee was authorized to negotiate and execute a lease subject to legal counsel review. Mrs. Alic said the project would likely serve mostly private use. Yes: 6 (Anne, Hauff, Haupt, Philippart, Schmidt, Wilson). No: 1 (Alic).

**Public Comment and Board Comments**
Fifteen speakers addressed the Board under non-agenda public communication, limited to one minute each to allow a full hour; all but one spoke against removal of the honors program. Board members reported on the TSD Business Education Roundtable, the NSBA Conference, and the district art show. The next workshop was announced for Tuesday, May 2nd at the Administration Building and the next regular meeting for Tuesday, May 16th at 7:00 pm at the Services Building.
2023_038_m041823bdmtg.verbose:
Minutes of a regular meeting of the Board of Education, Troy, Michigan, held April 18, 2023 at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois. President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. In addition to Mr. Schmidt, present were Board members Alic, Anne, Hauff, Haupt, Philippart, and Wilson. Also present were Superintendent Machesky and administrators Birmingham, DiPilato, Griffor, Detmer, Duda, Roncone, Jansen, Canfield, Griffin, Naus, Cottone, Young, Henry, Barsh, Keen, Recker, DiPonio, Keyser, Conaton, Harris, and West. There were approximately 150 members of the audience. The minutes are signed by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary, Troy Board of Education, and bear the notation GH/jh.

RECOGNITION. President Schmidt changed the order of the Recognition items on the agenda. The first item was the Mission Moment, recognizing the work of two teachers at Leonard Elementary School: ASD teacher Megan Murray and Literacy Specialist Nancy Haboush, who worked together to create an adapted version of LLI intervention, with the minutes describing its impact on students in the ASD room as nothing short of amazing. Dr. Erin Detmer and Sarah Young were invited up to introduce the teachers and share more about their work. The next item was the Student Spotlight, in which the Board recognizes the creative achievements of students in the TSD Creative Guild; Thomas Butcher was invited up to introduce Grace Cafagna, a senior at Athens High School, and share more about her special work.

Outstanding Support Staff. The Board recognized its Outstanding Support Staff employee of the year, a category that includes bus drivers, secretaries, paraprofessionals, student support aides, custodial staff, food service, technology, childcare, security and more. The district received 25 nominees for Outstanding Support Staff Employee of the Year. Stefanie Gervais was honored as the 2023 Outstanding Support Staff employee of the year. A short video clip was shared of the district's visit to surprise Stefanie, along with words from those who nominated her. She and the rest of the nominees were to be recognized at a reception on May 11th. Stefanie was invited up to say a few words to the Board and receive congratulations.

Outstanding Teachers. The Outstanding Teacher of the Year program received 62 nominations, with educators from every building nominated by families, students and colleagues at the preschool, elementary, middle, and high school levels. Four teachers were selected. A short video was shared of the district's administrative team surprising the winners in their classrooms. All nominees were to be recognized at a reception on April 25th, where they would receive their nomination packets, a small token of appreciation, and the chance to visit with those who nominated them. The four Outstanding Teachers for 2023 are: High School, Erich Beregszaszy, Science Teacher, Athens High School; Middle School, Shannon Dziwanowski, Science Teacher, Larson Middle School; Preschool, Patricia Grandy, Teacher, Troy Preschool; and Elementary, Karen Rosewarne, 5th Grade Teacher, Leonard Elementary School. Mrs. Rosewarne was also selected as the Overall TSD Teacher of the Year for 2023. The winners were sent to Oakland Schools to represent Troy in the Countywide Outstanding Teacher Award program.

ADDITIONS AND DELETIONS: None. PUBLIC COMMUNICATION (AGENDA ITEMS): None.

GENERAL, CONSENT AGENDA, Resolution 23-024. It was moved by Mr. Hauff and supported by Mr. Haupt that the Troy Board of Education approve items A, B, C, D, E, and F on the consent agenda: minutes of the March 7, 2023 Board of Education Workshop; minutes of the March 11, 2023 Board of Education Retreat; minutes of the March 21, 2023 Board of Education Meeting; the Treasurer's Report for February 2023; an Ancillary Fund(s) Budget Amendment; and rescheduling the June 20 Board meeting to June 13 at 7:30 pm with the meeting location changed to Troy High School. Yes: 7. No: 0.

PERSONNEL. Resolution 23-025, moved by Dr. Wilson and supported by Mr. Hauff: the Board issues a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure to Mr. Patrick Griffin, who will begin his duties as Principal, International Academy East effective July 1, 2023. Yes: 7. No: 0. Resolution 23-026, moved by Mrs. Anne and supported by Dr. Philippart: a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure to Ms. Gabrielle Naus, who will begin her duties as Assistant Principal, International Academy East effective July 1, 2023. Yes: 7. No: 0. Resolution 23-027, moved by Mr. Haupt and supported by Mrs. Alic: a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure to Mr. John Pagel, who will begin his duties as Assistant Superintendent, Employee Services effective July 1, 2023. Yes: 7. No: 0. Resolution 23-028, moved by Mrs. Alic and supported by Mrs. Anne: a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure to Mr. Brian Canfield, who will begin his duties as Director, Employee Services effective July 1, 2023. Yes: 7. No: 0. Resolution 23-029, under the heading Elementary and Secondary, moved by Dr. Philippart and supported by Dr. Wilson: the Board approves the personnel recommendations as stated, listing New Hire: Szczepanski. Yes: 7. No: 0.

CURRICULUM: None.

BUSINESS. Resolution 23-030, THS Gym Floor Renovation, moved by Mrs. Alic and supported by Mr. Hauff: the bid for gym floor renovation work be awarded to Floor Care Concepts in the amount of $63,930.00, with that amount approved as an expenditure of the Building Site & Sinking Fund and/or the 2023 Bond Fund. Yes: 7. No: 0. Resolution 23-031, Elementary Audio Upgrades, moved by Mr. Hauff and supported by Mr. Haupt: the bid for Elementary Audio Upgrades be awarded to TelSystems in the amount of $498,676.00, approved as an expenditure of the 2023 Bond Fund. Yes: 7. No: 0.

Resolution 23-032, Public-Private Partnership (Troy Racquet Club), moved by Mrs. Anne and supported by Dr. Philippart. The whereas clauses state that the School District and TRC desire to enter a Public-Private Partnership that positively impacts the students of Troy; that both desire to expand tennis and pickleball offerings to students of Troy School District and the community of Troy through development of a tennis facility on the Troy High School site; that the design of the facility and site will seek to minimize additional concrete and traffic flow issues; that the design will seek to minimize adverse environmental impact through retention of current trees or planting of new trees; that, subject to design and construction approval, the facility would include 12-15 tennis courts, an expansion of the 8 courts that currently exist; that, subject to design and construction approval, the facility would be domed approximately October through April to allow winter play and include outdoor lighting to allow later evening play in the summer; that the facility would be membership-based pay to play for community members and likewise for students outside of the school day; that Troy High School students and staff will have free exclusive access during tennis sections of the Physical Education curriculum; that Troy School District Tennis Programs will have free access during their season; that TRC will provide free membership and access to the club for Troy students who show proof of economically disadvantaged status; that the Board will explore additional sites and opportunities to provide free access to tennis for students and community through development of new tennis courts; and that the District desires to authorize the Superintendent, Dr. Richard Machesky, or his designee, to negotiate and execute a lease agreement with TRC consistent with the resolution, subject to review and approval by the School District's legal counsel. The resolved clause authorizes Dr. Machesky or his designee accordingly. Mrs. Alic explained why she would vote no, stating that while the project would provide some benefit to students it would likely serve mostly private use, and adding that although she was voting no she would support the Board's overall decision in moving forward on the partnership. Yes: 6 (Anne, Hauff, Haupt, Philippart, Schmidt, Wilson). No: 1 (Alic).

REPORTS FROM STUDENT REPRESENTATIVES. Sara Ali, student representative for Athens High School, reported on events and activities at Athens. Nish Palepu, student representative for Troy High School, was absent. Alexi Papadelis, student representative for Troy College and Career High School, reported on events at her school and announced Arts Beats & Treats on May 12th from 2:30 to 5:00 pm. Yara Mashal, student representative for International Academy-East, reported on events at her school and invited everyone to the Senior Art Show and Empty Bowls Dinner on April 25th.

PUBLIC COMMUNICATION (NON-AGENDA ITEMS). Mr. Schmidt explained the guidelines for public comment and informed the audience that due to the number of requests submitted, each person would have only one minute to speak, allowing a full hour of public comment. Mr. Joseph Olivier, TSD parent, addressed the Board regarding the Exchange Student Enrollment policy at Troy High and Athens. The following speakers addressed the Board regarding removal of the honors program and supported keeping that as an option for students: Mr. Toby Tang, TSD parent; Mr. Victor Li, 6th grade student at Boulan Park Middle School; Jing Dai, TSD parent; Hengguang Li, TSD parent; Krish Mathrani, junior at IA-East; Mr. Carol Toppi, TSD parent; Mr. Andrew Sosnoski, TSD parent; Ms. Yue (Luna) Xuan, TSD parent; Mr. Steven Sheng, TSD parent; Amy Luo, TSD parent; Le Xia, TSD parent; Mark Gunn, Troy community member who ran for state representative in the 2022 elections; Yan Liang, TSD parent; and Mr. Shan Jiang, TSD parent.

OTHER: None.

BOARD MEMBER COMMENTS. Dr. Philippart described attending the TSD Business Education Roundtable meeting that week and thanked the TSD administration, Doug Tietz, Corewell Health, Magna, and AT&T for participating, speaking about public/private partnerships and project-based learning as an opportunity for students to experience the world of work. Mrs. Anne said she attended the NSBA Conference, where she learned about student voice and the possibility of students having outside mentors. Mrs. Alic noted that Ramadan was coming to a close and wished everyone a belated Happy Passover. Mr. Hauff spoke about the importance of celebrating fine arts and said he visited the Art Show at the Troy Community Center. Dr. Wilson discussed events being showcased around the District and said the Art Show would be open until May 3rd; she thanked the community for voicing concerns and opinions and invited them to watch the District's YouTube channel for recorded Community Conversations about upcoming curriculum changes. Mr. Schmidt announced the next Board Workshop for Tuesday, May 2nd at the Administration Building and the next regular meeting for Tuesday, May 16th at 7:00 pm at the Services Building.

ADJOURNMENT. The meeting adjourned at 9:20 p.m.
